   o Presentation on the Determination of Capacityfor Parkers Ptace LLC Proposed
       Devetopment

Chairman Dan Cunningham catted this Pubtic Hearing on the proposed Water rates to order at 6:30
PM. He read the Notice of Pubtic Hearing and noted that it was pubtished in the New London Day
newspaper on 09/1 3/24 and 09/18124 (Exhibit A).

Chairman Cunningham catted for the appticant to present.
Attorney Harry Hetter f rom Uncasvitte Cl representing the Appticant, Parkers Ptace LLC, stated that
the apptication is for attocation of sewer capacity for 60 proposed affordabte housing rentaI units in
two buitdings of 30 units each. lf this attocation is granted, the appticant witt request a second
hearing to pursue the proposaI of retocation of the sewer shed tine to the property's edge to
accommodate the second phase of the project for two more buil.dings.
Attorney Hetter mentioned that the portion of the property proposed for devetopment is map is in
the Coast Management Area. A copy of the GIS System that show the sewer shed area and the
Coast Management Area was introduced into the record (Exhibit E). There is a state poticy to avoid
devetopment within the coastaI zone that woutd need septic systems. The apptication to sewer with
this project is consistent with the state's poLicies.
Attorney Hetler atso introduced a Location Guide Map and guidetines from the Connecticut Ptan of
Conservation and Devetopment (Exhibit F)- the property, represented by a dot on the map, is
tocated within a Priority Funding Area. Such areas are under the State Conservation and
Devetopment's prioritized for devetopment and state funding.
Parkers Ptace LLC is a singte member timited tiabitity company, the principat of which is Jason
Pazzaglia. Jason is atso the sole member of the LLC know as Bride Lake LLC. Bride Lake LLC is
devetoping a 100-unit affordabte housing which has been granted a sewer capacity attocation of
33,500 gal.lons. As of June 3A,2024,38 units in Bride Lake have been occupied for a period of six
months. Statistical. data of water usage was introduced to the record that tists the average usage of
gatLons of water per day (Exhibit G). Attorney Hetter noted that an average of 82 gatl.ons of water per
day is used at Bride Lake with an average of 35 gattons of water per day per bedroom (2- and 3-
bedroom units). Since 33,500 gatLons has been attocated for sewer capacity, based on the usage
data, the anticipation is that onty 10K to 12K onl.y wittthe needed at that location. Attorney Hetter
asked that Commission would consider shifting some of the attocation for sewer capacity from the
Bride Lake location to the Parkers Ptace project. Attorney Hetter atso provided statisticatdata from
the Groton Utitities for at[ water consumers for the town of Ledyard (Exhibit H). He noted that the
average usage of water per househotd per day is 153 gattons (average of 53 gattons per day per
bedroom) in Ledyard. This data was used in comparison to the Bride Lake usage to exemptify how
the state's guidetines of 150 gattons per day per bedroom coutd be outdated.
Attorney Hetter reiterated that based on at[ the data, the 60 units at Parkers Ptace would need about
12K gatton atlocation for sewer capacity. Atso, this devetopment woutd hetp atteviate the scarcity of
affordabte housing in the area. He asked that the Commission would consider the request of
a[[ocation for Parkers Ptace.

Mr. Roberts asked for a summarization of the request. Attorney Hetter responded that based on the
statistical data provided to the Commission, the sewer usage at Bride Lake witt probabty be 15,000
gal.tons instead of the atlocated amount of 33,500 gattons. Using that assumption, Parkers Ptace

Mrs. Russett asked if the EL Water and Sewer Dept. is tegatty bound to the State's guidetine of 1 50
gattons per day per bedroom. Mr. Norh responded that the EL Water and Sewer Dept. has adopted

Mrs. WiLtiams asked Attorney Tamarka what the tegat imptications are on devetopers requesting to
shift approved attocations of sewer from one development to other ptanned development.
Attorney Zamarka responded that he would have to do some research into it before any decisions
are made.
Mrs. Wittiams had concerns about the Bride Lake data since not at[ units are buitt or occupied.
Attorney Hetter responded that 50 units are occupied but the data was cotlected for 38 units for six
months.

Mr. Bond asked Mr. North if the Town has a method/regutation to recapture assigned sewer capacity
that is not being used after years of usage. Mr. North responded that reattocation of sewer capacity
is not something that has been considered before. Mr. Bond said that maybe reattocation woutd
atleviate the impending sewer capacity timitation.
Mr. Murphy questioned that about 200/o ol the units of the Bride Lake Development used
significantty more water than the rest. Attorney Hetl,er agreed that the data at Bride Lake was timited
therefore the data from Groton Utitities was also presented.

Mr. Roberts asked the Town Councitwhat the options for would be for tonight. Atty Zamarka
responded that the Publ,ic Hearing session's purpose was to turn in evidence and testimonies into

Wil.iams and Mr. Bond had presented other questions, it is suggested that once the Pubtic Hearing
is concLuded, that any del.iberations shoutd be postponed to the next meeting. Attorney Hetter
requested since Mr. North woutd [ike more statisticaI data, that the Pubtic Hearing stays open.

Mrs. Wittiams asked for ctarif ication if the request was for altocation or reattocation of sewer
capacity. Attorney Hetler responded that if there is avaitabte capacity to be assigned than it is an
attocation. lf the capacity is not avaitabte, then it is a reattocation from what had been assigned to
Bride Lake.

Mr. North distributed the foltowing exhibits:
         -  Notice of Pubtic Hearing and noted that it was pubtished in the New London Day

          APPLICATIONS FOR DETER INATION OF ADEQUACY OF
      SEWER GAPACITY PURSUANT TO GENERAL STATUTES $7-246a(aX1)

Sewage treatment for the Town of East Lyme is limited. Pursuant to an agreement with
the City of New London and Town of Waterford, East Lyme is currently entitled to a
maximum of 1.5 million gallons per day of sewer ireatment capacity at the New London
Regional Water Pollution Control Facility. ln order to ensure that there is adequate
capacity for all customers, the Commission adopts the following regulation for
applications for sewer treatment capacity pursuant to General Statutes S7-246a(aXl ).

      Aoolication. For all development projects that either (a) request a connection for
         more than 20 residential units or (b) require more than 5,000 gallons per day
         of sewage treatment capacity, an application, pursuant to General Statutes
         $7-246a(a)(1), for determination of adequacy of sewer capacity related to a
         proposed use of land, shall be submitted to the East Lyme Water and Sewer
         Commission ("Commission") on a form satisfactory to the Commission, and
         shall include all of the following:

       1. A class A-2 survey of the property to be developed showing the general
          layout of the proposed use of land:

       2. Proof that the applicant owns the property to be developed, or has the right to
          develop the property, and

       3 Documentation supporting the amount of capacity being requested
              a   Documentation related to a proposed residential development shall
                  include the number of residential units, the numbers of bedrooms per
                  unit and the methodology used in calculating the amount of capacity
                  being requested.

              b. Documentation related to a proposed non-residential or commercial
                  development shall include the methodology used in calculating the
                  amount of capacity being requested, and any special circumstances
                  (i.e the type of sewage being treated, design specifications, etc ) that
                  would affect the amount of capacity being requested.

              c. The Commission reserves the right to request from an applicant such
                  other information that it deems necessary.




                                                I
                                                                                            g
                                                                                    er\''br\
                                                                                        (%" P-,
   4. A non-refundable application fee of $500.00 shall be paid when an application
         is submitted. An additional public hearing fee of $450.oo may be assessed if
         applicable.



ll. Duration
   1   . Within 12 months after the expiration of the appeal period of a capacity
         allocation, the applicant shall (1) apply for all necessary land use approvals
         for the proposed use of land, and (2) provide proof of all such applications to
         the Commission. lf an applicant fails to apply for alt necessary land use
         approvals, or fails to provide proof of such applications to the Commission
         within this 12-month period, the sewer capacity allocated to the applicant shall
         terminate and be considered null and void.

   2 lf the applicant fails to obtain all land use approvals required for the proposed
         use of land, the sewer capacity allocated to the applicant shall terminate and
         be considered null and void.

   3. The Commission will notify an applicant in writing when an allocation has
         terminated. The failure of the Commission to provide written notice in a timely
         manner shall not constitute or be construed as a waiver of the Commission's
         right to declare a terminated allocation null and void

    4. A capacity allocation shall be in etfect for a period not to exceed 48 months
         from the expiration of the appeal period of the applicant's last land use
         approval with no appeal having been taken therefrom or an unappealed
         decision of a court of competent jurisdiction adjudicating such land use
         appeal The Commission may extend an allocation of sewer capacity beyond
         4 years if it determines, in its sole discretion, that good cause exists.

       5. lf the amount of sewer treatment capacity needed by an applicant decreases
          during the land use approval process, the applicant shall notify the
          Cornm ission immediately.

 lll Public Hearinq The Commission may, in its sole discretion, hold a public hearing
          on any application. Any such public hearing shall be in accordance with the
          provisions of General Statutes 8-7d.

 lV. Criteria. ln making a decision on an application the Commission may consider,
         without limitation, the following:

       Need for service in the proposed development area

                                                                                    P"bo 3
   Other pending applications and areas in town designated for sewer service

   Pollution abatement and public health

   Limitations and policies for sewer service

   Local and state Plans of Conservation and Development

   Effect of inflow and infiltration on available capacity

   whether the proposed development area can be serviced by other means

   Whether the proposed development area is within the East Lyme Sewer Service
   District

   Size of property proposed to be developed

   Remaining sewered and unsewered land area of town

   Effect of the allocation on remaining capacity

   Safe design standards of the East Lyme sewer system

V. Prior Requlation. This Regulation shall supersede the lnterim Sewer Connection
       Procedure adopted by the Commission on September 2b, 2018.

In accordance with CGS Section 16a-35c(b). oPM "shall develop recommendations for delineation

The LGM continues to be based on the same criteria from the LGM adopted as
                                                                                part of the 2013-2018

State C&D plan. In order to address shortcomings associated with the use of
                                                                            Census-defined Unban
                                                                              Blocks that meet any ftao
Area or Urban Cluster, Priority Funding Areas are now classified by Census
or more of the following criteria:
    o Designation as an urban Area or urban Cluster in the 2010 census
    . Are within al/zmilebuffer surrounding existing or planned mass-transit stations (rail and
        busway)
    r Contain existing or planned sewer service from an adopted Wastewater Facility Plan
    o Contain existing or planned water service from an adopted Public Drinking Water SupplyPlan
    r Contain a local bus route that provides bus service not less than 7 days a week

                                                                                   require state
 An intended outcome of this delineation of Priority Funding Area boundaries is to
 agencies to consider the municipal plan of conservation and development,
                                                                          in accordance with CGS


                                                                                                    Page | 25
Section 16a-35c1, whenever they propose to site a growth-related project in areas with only one or
none of the Priority Funding Area criteria.


Bolqnced Priority Funding Areos
Balanced Priority Funding Areas meet the criteria of both Priority Funding Areas and
Conservation Areas. State agencies that propose certain actions in these areas must provide balanced
consideration of all factors in determining the extent to which it is consistent with the policies of the
State C&D Plan. For example, a state-sponsored growth-related project (e.g., business expansion)
proposed in a Balanced Priority Funding Area that is also characterized as a Drinking Water Supply
Watershed would need to consider the integrity of the drinking water supply in determining the
consistency of its proposed action. In such cases, the sponsoring state agency shall consult with
                                                                                                  the

appropriate resource consultation agency or agencies (see below chart) to resolve any potentialpolicy
conflicts.


Village Priority Funding Areas
In the state's more rural municipalities, traditional village centers are considered to be Village
priority Funding Areas. This LGM classification is intended to recognize the unique characteristics
and needs of these areas, in accordance with CGS Section 16a-35e. Village Priority Funding Areas
were carried over from the 201g-20L8 State C&D Plan, and have been updated based on municipal
input.


Conservolion Areos
Conservation Areas are delineated based on the presence of factors that reflect environmental
                                                                                                   or

natural resource values. In contrast to Priority Funding Areas, which are based on man-made
                                                                                              as soils or
Census Blocks, Conservation Areas are based on existing environmental conditions, such
elevation, which oftentimes have no visible boundaries. Any growth-related project being
considered by a state agency in Conservation Areas would require an exception in accordance
                                                                                            with
                                                                                            plan of
CGS Section 16a-35ci. including a review of consistency with the affected municipality's
conservafi on and develoPment.
